transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, student health actually sent me here. They said my weight is too low to clear me for the youth workshops I wanted to help with. I guess the number has kept dropping recently, but... I don't know, to me it just feels like what naturally happens when I’m really focused and busy with things.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Yes, I am. Honestly, just the thought of gaining even a single pound makes me panic. If I were to eat a regular dinner, or, you know, something cooked with butter, I feel like everyone would immediately be able to tell. It would just look like I've completely lost my discipline.
Do you ever eat an amount of food that feels excessive to you in a short period of time?

No, not really. I mean, I don't ever eat large amounts of food like that. If anything, I'm just trying to stick to my safe foods and keep things controlled. I don't have moments where I lose control and eat a lot at once.
Do you think your weight is currently at a healthy level?

I mean, I know people keep saying it's dangerous, but honestly, that feels pretty exaggerated to me. I don't think it's as bad as they make it out to be. It just feels like everyone is making my body into this big problem, when really I'm just trying to stay sharp for school and my work. So, yeah, I think I'm fine.
Do you think you look too thin or underweight when you see yourself in the mirror?

No, I don't think I look too thin. Actually, when I look in the mirror, or... like, when I look at photos from my art showcase, I don't even really see the artwork first. I just zoom right in on my arms and my waist. If I look small enough in those pictures, I just feel like I'm serious and put-together. It doesn't look like I'm underweight to me, it just looks like I'm doing things right.
Have you ever eaten an amount of food that felt excessive to you?

Um, I think you asked me something like that a little bit ago, but... no, I haven't. Like I said before, I don't eat large amounts of food at all. I keep everything pretty strictly controlled, so eating excessively just isn't really something that happens.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating?
No, I don't do that. I don't really need to, since I'm pretty careful about what I eat in the first place. So, making myself throw up isn't something I do.
Do you exercise a lot?
Um, no, I don't really exercise. I don't go to the gym or do any kind of actual workout routine or anything. I just... I stick to managing my food, so working out isn't really something I focus on.
Do you use laxatives or diuretics to help control your weight?
No, I don't use anything like that. Like I said, I just control what I eat, so I don't take pills or anything to try and lose weight.
Have you ever felt like you lost control while eating?

No, not at all. I always know exactly what I'm having. I don't think I've ever just... lost control and eaten without thinking. Like I was saying, I'm very strict with myself, so feeling out of control with food really isn't something that happens to me.
When you think about gaining weight, what specifically worries you about how your body would look?

Honestly, just the idea of gaining even a single pound makes me panic. It's like... if I were to eat a normal dinner, or something with butter in it, I just feel like it would instantly show on my body. And my biggest worry is that everyone will be able to look at me and see that I've completely lost my discipline.
Do you think your friends or family see you as being underweight?

Yeah, they definitely do. I mean, I know people keep saying my weight is dangerous, but... it really feels exaggerated to me. It's like they're making my body into this huge problem, when honestly, I'm just trying to stay sharp for school and my work. I just don't see it as being as bad as they make it out to be.
Is your fear of gaining weight mostly about how you think your body would look to others?

I guess it's a mix of both. It is about what others see, but it's mostly about what it means to me. Like... when I look at photos from our recent showcase, I don't really see the artwork first. I immediately zoom in on my arms and my waist. And if I look small enough in the pictures, I feel like I'm serious and put-together. Gaining weight would just ruin that feeling.
When you look in the mirror, do you see yourself as being the same weight as others see you?

No, I... I don't think I do. Like I said before, my family thinks I'm dangerously thin, but when I look in the mirror, I just don't see what they're seeing. I see... well, I just see normal. Or honestly, I still see parts of my body that look too big to me. It's kind of confusing, because they act like I'm this fragile thing, but that's just not the reflection I'm looking at.
Is your fear of gaining weight also because you feel like you would lose control over your eating or your body if you were to gain weight?

Yeah, it is. It's very much about control. Honestly, even just the idea of gaining a single pound makes me panic. It feels like... if I were to sit down and eat a normal dinner, or have something with butter in it, everyone would instantly be able to see that I've lost my discipline. So, yeah, gaining weight feels like a complete loss of control over myself.
Do you think your weight or body shape is the main thing that determines your self-worth?

Yeah, I definitely do. It's, um, kind of like what I was saying earlier about those photos from my showcase. The art I made doesn't even really factor into how I feel about myself. I just look at the pictures and immediately check my arms and my waist. Because if I look small enough, then I feel like I have value... like I'm a serious, put-together person. If I wasn't thin, I don't think my art or anything else I do would even matter to me. So, yeah, my body shape is pretty much everything.
Is your fear of gaining weight because you think it would change how you perceive your body's appearance?

Um, I'm not really sure if that's it. I haven't really thought about it like that... like, whether gaining weight would change how I actually perceive myself. I just know that the thought of getting bigger is terrifying to me. But I haven't really noticed it being about my perception changing, if that makes sense. I just... I just really don't want the number to go up.
Do you think your fear of gaining weight is because you have a distorted view of what your body actually looks like?

I don't think so. I mean, I don't feel like my view is distorted. When I look in the mirror, I see what's actually there. I just... I just don't like what I see unless I'm at a certain weight. So, no, I don't think it's because I'm seeing things wrong, I just know what I need to look like to feel okay.
Have you ever felt like you've eaten an amount of food that's much larger than most people would eat in a similar time period?

No, I don't think so. I mean... I usually try to eat as little as possible, so I've never really had a time where I felt like I ate a huge amount of food. Definitely not more than what other people would eat in one sitting. It's pretty much always the opposite for me.
